title: Island Escape
story: Four safe islands sit at the corners of the space. Everyone else is at sea, and one shark decides who gets caught.
setup: Mark four small islands (hoops, flat squares of cones, or field corners) at the corners of a half-pitch. One coach or player starts as the shark in the middle.
instructions: Players move freely between islands; they are safe only while standing on one.
Players may stay on an island for a maximum of 5 seconds before they must move again.
The shark tries to tag players who are off an island.
A tagged player freezes at the center on one foot until a teammate runs past and taps them free.
Rotate the shark every 60-90 seconds so every player gets a turn.
coach_lens: Notice who waits for a safe gap versus who leaves on impulse, and who checks around them before committing to a run.
questions: How do you decide when it is safe to leave an island?
What did you see before you ran?

simplify: Allow a longer stay on each island.
Use a walking shark for the first round.
challenge: Shrink the islands or add more distance between them.
low_attendance: Use three islands instead of four so islands stay close together.
high_attendance: Add islands and a second shark rather than crowding the existing ones.
limited_equipment: Use shoes, jackets or field lines to mark islands.

safety: Tag with an open-hand touch only; no grabbing, pushing or blocking a path.
Keep islands far enough apart that players do not collide changing direction.

source.title: Children's Football Training Vision
source.reviewer_notes: Coach-authored safe-zone tag game developed and field-tested with a real youth team, applying DFB guidance on playful small games, individual challenges and free decision-making. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
